extracted.intended_audience: startup founders and early-stage communications leads
extracted.subtask_description: Practical playbook for founding teams to plan, write, and execute PR and press releases across pre-launch, launch, and sustained-growth phases. Emphasizes story types, distribution tactics, timing, and quality signals founders should hit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat PR as strategy, not validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders treat PR as validation, not strategy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PR to advance business objectives rather than chasing coverage for prestige. Align press activity to product-market fit and company milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't hire PR firms before product-market fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring PR firms before product-market fit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid outsourcing narrative and outreach too early; internal clarity on product and customers should precede agency engagement to prevent misaligned pitches and wasted spend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch the right outlets with the right stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitching the wrong outlets with the wrong stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match story type and angle to each outlet's audience and coverage area rather than blasting generic announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be consistent — avoid sporadic bursts
rubrics_metrics.description: Being inconsistent — sporadic instead of sustained
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan a sustained cadence of news and commentary rather than one-off announcements to build ongoing reporter relationships and audience familiarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand what reporters want
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be a useful source: provide context, data, customer proof, and timely exclusives tailored to reporters' beats to increase pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build relationships with reporters (10 in your space)
rubrics_metrics.description: Build relationships with 10 reporters in your space
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively cultivate a set of roughly ten reporters relevant to your domain; be a helpful source on their stories to establish trust before pitching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Become a useful source on others' stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Become a useful source on others' stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer data, commentary or introductions to help reporters on adjacent topics; reciprocity builds rapport for future exclusives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop your founder voice publicly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share perspective and thought leadership publicly (e.g., LinkedIn, bylines) so reporters can understand and quote founder POVs authentically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish company website and newsroom
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a central place with releases, boilerplate, press contacts, and assets to make reporters' jobs easier and to control the canonical story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan launch 3–6 months in advance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate product, legal, executive availability, embargo plans, and outreach schedule well before the announced launch date to maximize coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief 2–3 trusted reporters under embargo
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer embargoed exclusives to a small set of trusted outlets to secure prominent coverage and shape the initial narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate same-day distribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure simultaneous publication across planned outlets and channels to concentrate attention and avoid staggered dilution of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare founder for media days
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coach founders on key messages, likely questions, and concise, specific quotes to make interviews high-impact and on-message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have newsworthy moments every 4–6 weeks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a cadence of fresh, timely news or commentary to keep momentum with reporters and audiences (product updates, customer wins, commentary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish data reports quarterly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create proprietary data or industry reports on a quarterly basis to generate recurring media interest and original story angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use customer wins as pitch material
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage measurable customer outcomes and stories (with metrics and quotes) to demonstrate product value and newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue industry commentary opportunities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position founders or company spokespeople as go-to commentators for industry trends to build credibility beyond product announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in founder thought leadership
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop opinion pieces, bylines, and public commentary from founders to elevate brand and create reporter touchpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin story — rich detail and founder voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the founding narrative with specificity and personal voice; include obstacles, motivations, and unique insights that make the story compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer transformation with metrics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame customer case studies with before/after metrics and concrete outcomes rather than vague testimonials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry data report with proprietary insight
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share exclusive data or analysis that reveals trends, market size, or surprising findings to create a unique story hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pivot story with honest learnings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When announcing a pivot, explain why, what was learned, and how the new direction is supported by evidence and customer signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring announcement only if person is famous
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring announcement (only if person is famous)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid routine hiring press unless the hire is high-profile enough to be newsworthy; otherwise fold hiring into broader company narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitive market analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer contrarian data-backed takes that challenge assumptions in the industry to attract analytical coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline must combine news and a specific number
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft headlines that immediately communicate the news and quantify it (e.g., users, revenue, growth) to convey concreteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: one sentence news + one sentence stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Lede: One sentence with the news; one sentence with stakes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a tight two-sentence lede that tells what happened and why it matters to readers or the market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: include context, methodology, customer proof
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how results were obtained, provide supporting data and customer quotes, and situate the announcement within broader market context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote: founder voice, specific, avoid clichés
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote: Founder voice, specific, no clichés
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quotable, concrete statements from founders that reveal perspective and add value beyond the factual lede; avoid generic platitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: 50 words describing what you do and scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate: 50 words, what you do + scale
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep company boilerplate concise (~50 words) and include mission, primary offering, and scale/traction metrics where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact: founder direct or head of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact: Founder direct OR head of communications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a direct, responsive contact for reporters—either the founder or head of comms—to facilitate follow-ups and interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use embargoed exclusive to top trade outlet
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoed exclusive to top trade outlet
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer one high-value outlet an embargoed exclusive to secure a marquee story ahead of broader distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate release to 5–10 secondary outlets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a targeted secondary list and time distribution to maximize coverage across relevant verticals following the exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the wire for SEO after initial coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish to wire services after top outlets have run the story to capture search traffic without undermining exclusive relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder LinkedIn post same day
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have the founder amplify the coverage via LinkedIn (or other platforms) concurrently to drive attention and social proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsletter inclusion when relevant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target newsletters where the audience aligns with your story to extend reach and acquire engaged readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcements must state use-of-funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding announcements with no use-of-funds clarity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always explain how new capital will be deployed; vague funding press releases reduce credibility and reporter interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid CEO quotes that say 'we are excited'
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes from CEO that say "we are excited"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace generic enthusiasm with specific comments about impact, strategy, or measurable outcomes to be quote-worthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't include customer logos without context
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer logos without quotes or context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you display customer logos, pair them with quotes or case details to prove real engagement rather than name-dropping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague 'first' or 'largest' claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only make comparative claims when verifiable; unsupported superlatives invite skepticism and reduce credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wire-only distribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying solely on wire distribution leads to low impact; prioritize targeted outreach and exclusives to earn meaningful coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained PR cadence (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate PR by recurring, planned news and engagement rather than isolated announcements; cadence signals seriousness and momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder voice present in quotes (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality releases feature authentic founder voice in quotes that add perspective beyond the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match story type to startup stage (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific story types matching startup stage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose story types appropriate to maturity—e.g., origin or product stories pre-launch; data reports and customer transformations for scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer embargoed exclusives (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embargoed exclusives strategically to secure top-tier coverage and shape narrative control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder availability for interviews (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure founders are accessible and prepared to speak with reporters promptly; unavailability harms pickup and depth of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make honest, verifiable claims (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantiate assertions with data, methodology, or customer proof to maintain credibility with journalists and readers.
